meta.description: Polls a Gmail mailbox and pushes each new message through SHIPMATE's reader. Replaces v2's Microsoft Graph leg with Gmail for the demo. The Gmail credential is authorised once in n8n's own UI — nothing here holds a Google token.

nodes.name: New mail
nodes.notes: Click Connect on the credential and authorise your Google account once. n8n stores the token; SHIPMATE never sees it. Attachments are off — the reader works on text, and a 10MB packing list through a webhook helps nobody.

nodes.name: SHIPMATE /email/ingest
nodes.notes: SHIPMATE decides whether this is an enquiry and whether it is confident enough to act. Most mail comes back acted:false with a reason, which is the point — a newsletter must not become a customer record. Ingest is idempotent on messageId, so a re-poll costs nothing.

nodes.name: Re-sweep the board
nodes.notes: A new commitment changes the risk picture straight away, so the desk sees it now rather than at the next cron tick.

parameters.content:
## Drafting a reply

`POST /email/draft` returns a reply body for a message, with an optional `instruction` in the operator's own words ("tell them space is confirmed, ask for the packing list").

It is deliberately **not** wired to a Gmail send node here. Sending mail on a customer's behalf is a human's decision, and a draft that posts itself the moment a model produces it is how a wrong rate reaches a real consignee.

Add a send node only behind an approval step.

nodes.name: Is this an RFQ reply?
nodes.notes: Tried first. A partner's reply to a rate request is mail like any other — what makes it an RFQ answer is that its threadId matches an outstanding row in partner_quotes. If it matches nothing, SHIPMATE says matched:false and the mail falls through to the enquiry reader. Nothing is guessed at.
